newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Trelleborg shares up but off highs.
newsitem.headline: Trelleborg shares up but off highs.

text.p: Shares in Swedish metals and mining company Trelleborg AB came off day highs after news that its mining subsidiary Boliden will set up a joint venture with Adolf Lundin's company South Atlantic Resources.
But the shares were still higher than at the close on Friday.
At 1335 GMT, the share was up 2.5 crowns at 111, after touching 114 crowns ahead of Boliden's press conference.
"Ahead of the news, there were speculation about a change in Boliden's ownership structure or a spin-off and separate listing of the company," a broker said.
"The joint venture was an initial disappointment and the share came off highs, but later rebounded some as players still saw the news as one step toward a change in Trelleborg's structure," he said.
He added, however, that the near term development of the share largely would depend on analysis of the deal.
